cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Put It Back Quietly
cards.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your plate is back in the cupboard. Set it down gently, please; rims chip when you drop one plate onto another.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Our plates are plain. That one has flowers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then this is the serving plate. We distinguish serving pieces from place settings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need all six plain plates for Sunday. Where's the sixth?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll supply six matching floral ones. Put the plain ones at the back, please. A proper table uses one service; let's get that right first.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 handling care, A3 serving/place-setting distinction and A5 one-service rule let A professionally normalise a substitute without admitting the original loss.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 flowers cause A3 reclassification; B4 missing plain sixth causes A5 a full floral replacement and storage instruction.

relationship.evidence: B2 recognises household crockery and B4 needs six matching settings, forcing A beyond the first excuse.

heightening.evidence: A5 expands one discrepant returned plate into a complete new set to evade B4 missing-original question.

specificity.evidence: A1 returned plate, B2 original pattern and B4 six-count make the concealed replacement legible.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 one-service correction directs the Sunday setup and avoids a detached account of the cover-up.
